    FAPD-AI: A defendant appealed his convictions for both receiving and possessing child pornography under a Double Jeopardy Clause argument.     Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-26-01321 / USCOURTS-ca10-26-01321-0

    FAPD-AI: A defendant in a civil rights case appealed the district court's perceived delay in ruling on its motion for summary judgment based on qualified immunity. The court dismissed the appeal for lack of jurisdiction, finding that the defendant failed to identify a specific district court order as the subject of the appeal and that no actual order denying the motion existed. The court noted that the district court expressly stated it would issue a decision on the motion in due course and that delay alone does not constitute a reviewable denial of qualified immunity defense.     FAPD-AI: A consolidated appeal addressed lawsuits by survivors and families of Club Q nightclub shooting victims against El Paso County and Club Q defendants.     United States v. Miranda-Espinoza (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-25-06166 / USCOURTS-ca10-25-06166-0

    FAPD-AI: A defendant appealed his 84-month sentence for illegal reentry after prior deportations as substantively unreasonable, claiming an unwarranted sentencing disparity. The court affirmed, finding the district court adequately considered statutory factors including the defendant's conduct (domestic assault and battery by strangulation), prior deportations and illegal reentries, and criminal history. The court held that detailed reasoning for an individualized sentence assessment suffices even without national sentencing statistics. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: In November 2022, Anderson Aldrich opened fire in Club Q, an LGBTQIA+ nightclub in Colorado Springs, killing five people and injuring 25 others. Survivors and families sued the county and Club Q under federal and Colorado law. The Tenth Circuit affirmed dismissal of federal and Colorado Premises Liability Act claims but reversed on state negligence and wrongful-death claims, finding that Colorado's Premises Liability Act provides the exclusive remedy for injuries arising from Club Q's conditions.   • Observed at 20:30:42 Eastern time ET
    Black Emergency Response Team, et al v. Drummond, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-24-06141 / USCOURTS-ca10-24-06141-0

    FAPD-AI: Oklahoma's H.B. 1775, subsection B, prohibits public school employees from requiring or making part of a course eight specified concepts that would advocate race or sex discrimination. Teachers and students challenged the statute as violating First Amendment rights to receive information and as unconstitutionally vague. The Tenth Circuit reversed a preliminary injunction, holding that the statute unambiguously prohibits only teaching the concepts as correct principles, not discussing them in abstract or historical contexts, and therefore does not violate the vagueness doctrine. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-25-05806 / USCOURTS-ca6-25-05806-0

    FAPD-AI: The Sixth Circuit affirmed that an insurance policy's exclusion for professional services barred an insurer's duty to indemnify Seven Counties Services for a wrongful death claim arising from a behavioral care worker's physical restraint of a child. The court held that the restraint qualified as a professional service under the insurance contract even though it was negligently performed. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 17:56:17 Eastern time ET
    Vella, Et AL. V. Macd Helicopters, INC., Et AL. (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca9-25-2722 / USCOURTS-ca9-25-2722-0

    FAPD-AI: The Ninth Circuit affirmed the dismissal of a products liability lawsuit against Boeing for a 2022 helicopter crash owned and operated by the Huntington Beach Police Department, holding that the General Aviation Revitalization Act's 18-year statute of repose applied to the government-owned aircraft. The court rejected plaintiffs' argument that the statute exempted publicly-owned aircraft, finding that GARA's definition of "general aviation aircraft" contains no public-aircraft exception. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca5-24-60395 / USCOURTS-ca5-24-60395-0

    FAPD-AI: The Fifth Circuit held that Mississippi's law allowing ballot receipt up to five business days after the federal election day is preempted by federal statutes establishing a uniform federal election day for congressional and presidential elections. The court reversed the district court's judgment and remanded for further proceedings. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: Olson Joseph was convicted of firearm possession in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1) after officers detected a concealed weapon during a street stop. The appellate court held that § 922(g)(1) does not violate the Second Amendment, but found officers lacked reasonable suspicion to stop Joseph based solely on the concealed firearm following Florida's 2015 amendment to its concealed-carry statute, and therefore vacated his conviction and reversed the denial of his suppression motion.     FAPD-AI: Senator Kent Conrad introduced S. 1939, the Livestock Market Revitalization Act of 1996, with Senators Dorgan and Kerrey as cosponsors. The bill amends the Packers and Stockyards Act and Agricultural Marketing Act to establish federal reporting on livestock transactions, require daily market demand information for sellers, implement monitoring of market concentration and competitive behavior, and improve labeling and trade data dissemination.   • Observed at 03:27:01 Eastern time ET
    Political Contributions by Certain Investment Advisers (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION · FR-2026-09-10 / 2026-18424

    official summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission” or the “SEC”) is proposing to rescind the political contribution rule under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (the “Advisers Act”), which prohibits investment advisers from providing investment advisory services for compensation to a government client for two years after an adviser or any covered associate of the adviser makes a contribution to certain categories of elected officials or candidates, among other prohibitions. In the more than fifteen years since the rule was adopted, implementation challenges associated with the political contribution rule have resulted in a range of significant unintended consequences, including compliance practices among some investment advisers that may have had the effect of restricting all political contributions by the investment advisers and their employees. Market participants also have stated that the political contribution rule is burdensome, complex, and both lacks clarity and creates a de facto strict liability standard. [official summary truncated; see source] FR-SEL-02

    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION · FR-2026-09-10 / 2026-18468

    official summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Bell Textron Canada Limited Model 505 helicopters. This proposed AD was prompted by a quality escape affecting certain tailcone assemblies. This proposed AD would require replacing any tailcone assembly that has exceeded a certain life limit. Also, this proposed AD would require inspecting the tailcone assembly for gaps, and repetitively inspecting the tailcone assembly for loose, damaged, or missing fasteners. Depending on the results of these inspections, this proposed AD would require conducting further inspections and corrective actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-02

    Telecommunications Relay Service ASCII Format Requirement (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FEDERAL COMMUNICATIONS COMMISSION · FR-2026-09-10 / 2026-18478

    official summary: In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) amends its rules to eliminate the requirement that Text Telephone (TTY)-based Telecommunications Relay Services (TRS) be capable of communicating in the American Standard Code for Information Interchange (ASCII) format. By removing this outdated regulatory mandate, the Commission relieves TRS providers of the obligation to maintain costly and obsolete ASCII-compatible hardware and software systems. Eliminating this requirement will reduce inefficiencies, preserve the integrity of the TRS Fund, and allow providers to redirect resources toward modern relay technologies, all without adversely impacting functional equivalence for consumers who rely on TTY-based TRS. FR-SEL-01

    Decennial Census of the Population of Americans; Proposed Residence Criteria and Proposed Regulations for Demographic Q… (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE · FR-2026-09-10 / 2026-18481

    official summary: The Census Bureau is proposing to add two new parts to the Code of Federal Regulations governing the decennial census of population and housing. First, the Census Bureau is proposing to add a part outlining the residence criteria used for identifying each person's “usual residence,” as needed to determine whether and where to count them in the census of the population throughout the United States. Second, the Census Bureau is proposing to add a part establishing standards and restrictions for the inclusion of certain demographic questions on the decennial census short-form questionnaire and any other questionnaire used for the enumeration of the population. The Census Bureau is considering these two additions to better prioritize and fulfill its Constitutional mandate to count for apportionment the “whole number of persons in each State” based on the concept of “usual residence”—a process that factors in an element of allegiance but otherwise should be colorblind and should not be distorted in any way by questions about immaterial personal characteristics, such as race. [official summary truncated; see source] FR-SEL-02

    Reef Fish Fishery of the Gulf of America; 2027 Red Grouper Commercial Quota Retention (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE · FR-2026-09-10 / 2026-18484

    official summary: NMFS proposes to implement management measures described in a framework action under the Fishery Management Plan for the Reef Fish Resources of the Gulf (FMP), as prepared by the Gulf Council (Council). If implemented, this proposed rule would withhold a portion of the commercial allocation of Gulf of America (Gulf) red grouper for the 2027 fishing year in anticipation of the upcoming rulemaking to implement Amendment 63 to the FMP (Amendment 63). If implemented by NMFS, Amendment 63 would establish a pilot program for setting aside a portion of the red grouper commercial quota for a quota pool. This proposed rule would withhold a portion of the red grouper commercial quota for the 2027 fishing year in the amount necessary to establish that quota pool. This withheld quota would otherwise be allocated to shareholders in the Individual Fishing Quota program for Gulf grouper and tilefishes (GT-IFQ) program on January 1, 2027. FR-SEL-02

    In Situ Recovery Monitoring and Decommissioning Timeliness (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · NUCLEAR REGULATORY COMMISSION · FR-2026-09-10 / 2026-18504

    official summary: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) proposes to amend its regulations that govern the licensing of uranium mills and the disposition of tailings and waste that arise from the extraction and milling of uranium by issuing risk-informed requirements for groundwater protection at uranium in situ recovery (ISR) facilities. The NRC's current regulations are focused on conventional uranium milling and do not expressly address uranium extraction by the ISR process. Additionally, NRC proposes to amend its regulations that govern decommissioning timeliness for all licensees to provide additional flexibility for licensees to delay the initiation of decommissioning activities in situations where safety would not be impacted.     Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION · FR-2026-09-10 / 2026-18520

    official summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Dassault Aviation Model FALCON 7X, MYSTERE-FALCON 900, FALCON 900EX, FALCON 2000, and FALCON 2000EX airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reported occurrences of seats sliding without passenger input. The cabin seat track locking mechanism was found to jam in isolated conditions during taxi, take-off, and landing (TTOL). This proposed AD would require modifying or replacing each affected seat. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected seats. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-02

  • Observed at 03:27:01 Eastern time ET
    Airworthiness Directives; Bell Textron Canada Limited Helicopters (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION · FR-2026-09-10 / 2026-18522

    official summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Bell Textron Canada Limited (Bell) Model 206L, 206L-1, 206L-3, and 206L-4 helicopters with FAA Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) SR02684LA installed. This proposed AD was prompted by an event where a Bell Model 206L helicopter with FAA STC SR02684LA installed experienced moderate to severe vertical vibration, which resulted in damage to the tail boom of the helicopter. This proposed AD would require revising the Limitations section of the existing rotorcraft flight manual (RFM) for the helicopter to include a never-exceed-speed (V NE ) limitation and would require incorporating a rotorcraft flight manual supplement (RFMS) into the existing RFM. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-02

    Promoting Fair Competition in Livestock Markets and Expanding Market Access for American Meat Producers (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FR-2026-09-10 / 2026-18567

    FAPD-AI: Executive Order 14424 directs the Secretary of Agriculture to prioritize enforcement of the Packers and Stockyards Act and increase investigative capacity within the USDA, including coordination with the Department of Justice. The order directs actions to expand interstate shipment of meat products, including streamlining state participation in cooperative inspection programs, creating technical assistance for small processors, and modernizing meat inspection. The Secretary is directed to establish a USDA coordinator position and to establish a guaranteed loan program for small and regional beef processors. FR-SEL-03

  • Observed at 03:27:01 Eastern time ET
    Supporting America's Ranchers (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FR-2026-09-10 / 2026-18571

    FAPD-AI: Executive Order 14425 directs a comprehensive review of federal regulations, guidance, and policies affecting ranchers and requests recommendations for promoting financial viability and market access. The order directs the Secretary of the Interior to assess whether gray wolves and Mexican wolves have met delisting or downlisting criteria under the Endangered Species Act and, if criteria are met, to begin delisting proceedings. The order directs the Secretary of Agriculture to review authorities permitting mandatory country-of-origin labeling for beef products and provide economic analysis of such labeling. FR-SEL-03
